name: Brooklyn waterfront facing Lower Manhattan
location_description: An elevated spot on the Brooklyn side of the East River, above the waterfront piers, facing Lower Manhattan. The Library of Congress record names Brooklyn and the East River but gives no exact camera position.

media.title: New York skyline from Brooklyn
media.creator: Detroit Publishing Co.
media.rights: No known restrictions on publication, according to the Library of Congress.

targets.notes: The tall tower on the left with a bulbous mansard dome, a large arched opening below it and a lantern on top matches the Singer Building’s crown.
The pair of cupolas just left of the Woolworth Building fits the Park Row Building, which stood in front of it from this direction.
The tallest tower, a slender shaft with a pointed Gothic crown, is the Woolworth Building.
The dome with a lantern, between the Woolworth and Municipal Buildings, is in the expected direction of the New York World Building’s dome on Park Row.
The broad white block on the right with a tiered tower on its roof is the Municipal Building.

observations.notes: The Library of Congress dates the glass negative to between 1900 and 1920. The Woolworth Building, completed in 1913, appears finished, so the photograph probably dates from 1913 or later. No camera metadata survives with the item. Image boxes are fractions of the 1024 × 809 pixel Library of Congress copy.
